tagline: Software and game developer from northern Germany

skills.name: JavaScript
skills.use: The language I write most days. Everything from the form service at the office to the small script that draws this page runs on it, and I still enjoy how little ceremony it needs.

skills.name: TypeScript
skills.use: For the projects that outgrow a handful of files. The types catch the mistakes I would otherwise meet at runtime, and the editor suddenly knows what every object looks like.

skills.name: HTML
skills.use: Every interface I ship is hand-written markup. Semantic elements, forms that work without a script, and pages a screen reader can follow from top to bottom.

skills.name: CSS
skills.use: Custom properties, grid and a few animations, no framework and no build step. Dark mode is not an afterthought, it is a second set of variables.

skills.name: C#
skills.use: Picked it up two weeks ago for a desktop tool at the office. Still reading more than writing, but I like how much the compiler catches before anything runs.

skills.name: Luau
skills.use: The scripting language behind my Roblox games. Game logic, data stores, and the client-server split that every multiplayer feature has to respect.

skills.name: Node.js
skills.use: My server runtime of choice. One process, no external services, and a standard library that covers more with every release, from fetch to the built-in SQLite driver.

skills.name: Express
skills.use: Routing and middleware for the services I build. The handlers stay thin, the actual logic lives in plain modules that know nothing about HTTP.

skills.name: .NET
skills.use: Arrived together with C#. So far it is the framework under one desktop tool, and the tooling around it is what I am still getting used to.

skills.name: Roblox Studio
skills.use: Where the games get built, tested and published. Prototyping a mechanic there is faster than in most engines I have tried.

skills.name: SQLite
skills.use: One file per service, personal data encrypted before it is written. No database server to run, back up or upgrade.

skills.name: Docker
skills.use: Every service ships as one container and runs on our own hardware behind a reverse proxy. An update is a new image and a restart.

skills.name: Linux
skills.use: The servers run Linux. systemd timers, SSH, backups, and reading logs at odd hours when something does not come back up.

skills.name: Git
skills.use: Branches, pull requests and tagged releases, even when I am the only one on the project. The history is documentation I do not have to write twice.

skills.name: GitHub Actions
skills.use: Builds the release images and redraws this profile once a day. Pinned actions, a minimal token, and nothing that loads from a third party.
